messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High error rate detected for service=api-gateway region=eu-west-1 — 5xx spike + traffic drop. Pager oncall: @maya :rotating_light:

maya (oncall-sre): I’m on it, grabbing dashboard and request traces. seeing 35% 5xx across eu-west and latency 95p -> 3.2s.

li (netops): I see a large increase in cross-region egress for eu-west -> us-east in our flow logs. Could be routing fallback.

maya (oncall-sre): Confirmed: many requests from eu customers are being routed to us-east. That explains latency and errors. Starting triage.

tom (eng-runtime): Any recent rollout to routing-policy service? I pushed a minor fix yesterday but nothing that should affect region pins.

carla (platform): No route-policy changes in last 24h from platform side. I’ll check config history and pin-sync status.

maya (oncall-sre): Initial mitigation: enable fallback-mode=prefer-local on the steering proxy for eu-west to try to drive traffic back. Doing canary to one host.

ben (support): Heads-up — Support is getting customer DMs about slow API calls from EU. I’ll draft comms if we need an incident update.

li (netops): Running quick checks: nat-gateway failover events at 2027-03-22T09:07Z in eu-west-1a; AWS reported partial fabric maintenance. egress IPs flipped to another AZ, which our region-pin service interprets as a change and rebalanced pins. Looks like pin-sync propagated inconsistently causing oscillation.

maya (oncall-sre): That would explain it — the pin keys are at per-az granularity. If NAT failover moved egress, pins didn't follow synchronously.

carla (platform): Searching logs: pin-sync job had a 503 to etcd at 09:06 and retried; some replicas updated, others not. TTL for pins is 300s. With DNS caching TTL=60s and some clients caching longer, we get a mix of endpoints -> oscillation.

tom (eng-runtime): Suggestion: temporarily force all eu-west traffic to pinned region eu-west-1 (global fallback off) by injecting a routing override. This will stop cross-region steering while we fix pin-sync.

maya (oncall-sre): Agreed. Applying override now: `/bin/rtrctl apply --scope=org:europe --override=force-region:eu-west-1 --reason="egress/nat failover causing pin drift"`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: routing-override applied by maya (oncall-sre) at 2027-03-22T09:12Z — id=ovr-2391.

li (netops): Nice. After override, backend logs show majority of requests staying in eu-west. 5xx rate dropping.

maya (oncall-sre): Rolling out DNS guidance: issue temporary advisory to ops to TTL-bump downstream caches where possible. But we can't force client caches.

ben (support): Posting initial incident note to status page: "Partial routing disruption affecting EU traffic; mitigation in progress." Will tag customers with impacted SLAs.

carla (platform): Root cause hypothesis so far: upstream provider maintenance -> NAT egress IP failover -> pin-sync retries against etcd during transient 503 -> partial pin state writes -> inconsistent steering decisions -> cross-region oscillation compounded by DNS TTLs and client caches.

tom (eng-runtime): For longer-term fix we should: 1) make pin-sync writes atomic across replicas, 2) change pin granularity to region-level (not AZ), 3) add faster reconciliation when provider signals egress change, 4) increase pin TTL jitter to avoid synchronized expiries.

maya (oncall-sre): Can we hotfix pin-sync to retry with backoff and validate quorum before accepting writes? Carla, can you push an emergency config to require quorum for writes?

carla (platform): Pushing config to enforce quorum for pin updates now. Command: `kubectl -n platform set env pin-sync PIN_WRITE_QUORUM=true` — applying to 3 replicas.

incident-bot: config-change recorded by carla (platform) at 2027-03-22T09:22Z — changeset=cfg-442.

li (netops): Monitoring shows pin-sync errors drop to 0 after config. Routing stabilizing. 5xx back to baseline.

maya (oncall-sre): Good. Next step: revert the temporary override once stable. I’ll keep override for 15 more minutes, then revert and observe.

ben (support): External comms updated: "Mitigation implemented; performance returning to normal. Tracking root cause; postmortem to follow." Customers acknowledged. :thumbsup:

maya (oncall-sre): Reverting override now: `/bin/rtrctl revert ovr-2391`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: override ovr-2391 reverted by maya (oncall-sre) at 2027-03-22T09:33Z.

li (netops): After revert, traffic remains pinned to eu-west, no further oscillation. Confirming steady-state for 10m.

carla (platform): Logged remediation actions and followups: pin-sync hardening, change pin granularity proposal, add reconciliation hook for egress-change events, and lower DNS TTL recommendations for critical endpoints.

maya (oncall-sre): Incident summary for postmortem: brief outage caused by mismatched pin state during cloud egress failover leading to cross-region routing and elevated latency/errors. No data exfiltration. Customer impact: increased latency and elevated 5xx for ~22 minutes for subset of EU requests.

ben (support): Creating postmortem ticket and linking customers flagged during incident.

maya (oncall-sre): Closing pager. Thanks team. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: incident-closed: incident id inc-20270322-01 closed at 2027-03-22T09:42Z — duration 35m.
